channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Holds 218 floor as bulls eye 219 breakout
item.description: The GBP/JPY rotates for the third straight day, as a ‘bullish harami’ chart pattern opens the door for further upside, but intervention fears by Japanese authorities cap the cross-pair advance. The GBP/JPY trades at 218.17, unchanged.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Sideways range holds against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann expect USD/SGD to remain directionless in the near term, with intraday trading confined to a tight 1.2900–1.2925 band. Over the coming weeks, the pair is seen oscillating in a broader 1.2875–1.2955 range as earlier downside momentum has faded.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar rises as strong labor data and Middle East tensions lift Oil
item.description: Here is what you need to know for Friday, July 24:

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: BI uses incentives over hikes – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay reports Bank Indonesia kept the BI Rate at 5.75%, choosing targeted capital-flow incentives over further tightening to support the Indonesian Rupiah. BI cut hedging costs and improved macroprudential liquidity tools, echoing RBI’s playbook.

item.title: Australian Dollar trades under pressure amid strong US data
item.description: AUD/USD trades lower near the 0.6970 area on Thursday, giving back earlier gains as the US Dollar (USD) strengthens on the back of upbeat United States (US) labor market data and continued hostilities between the US and Iran.

item.title: Asia FX: Oil shock seen manageable – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu argues that Oil near $95 is a shock for Asian energy importers but not a trigger for a broad balance-of-payments crisis.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG lower highs structure holds, bears eye $55
item.description: Silver price dives over 3.80% on Thursday as the precious metals segment tumbles amid overall US Dollar strength and heightened risk aversion amid heightened tensions in the Middle East. The XAG/USD trades at $57.62 after hitting a weekly high of $60.94.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Bulls struggle below the 50-day SMA
item.description: AUD/USD edges lower on Thursday as a stronger US Dollar (USD) outweighs support from stronger-than-expected Australian employment data. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.6966, down 0.45% on the day.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Holds near fair value against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is tracking the broader US Dollar (USD) trend, with USD/CAD easing overnight then rebounding to trade nearly flat.

item.title: Swiss Franc hits 13-month low as rising Oil prices boost bets on Fed hike
item.description: USD/CHF climbs to its highest level since June 2025 on Thursday, supported by a broadly stronger US Dollar (USD) as the expanding war in the Middle East pushes Oil prices higher and strengthens Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike expectations.

item.title: Gold tumbles as sellers target $4,000
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) loses nearly 2% on Thursday as the US Dollar stages a comeback amid growing speculation that the White House may continue its campaign against Iran, which seems poised to prolong the Gulf war. The XAU/USD trades below $4,050 after falling from a two-day high above $4,100

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average sells the war without an earnings alibi
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades around 600 points lower on Thursday, down 1.1% near 51,600 in a session whose high sits within a handful of points of the opening print.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Bears target a break below 1.1350 support
item.description: EUR/USD trades on the back foot on Thursday as the expanding war in the Middle East pushes Oil prices higher and fuels hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations, boosting demand for the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Gold falls as Iran war lifts Oil prices, Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) loses ground on Thursday, snapping a four-day winning streak as the US Dollar (USD) rebounds, while the widening war in the Middle East drives Oil prices higher. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,050 after hitting a two-week high of $4,165 on Wednesday.

item.title: US President Trump: “I'm considering a massive attack greater than anything before”
item.description: US President Donald Trump said he is close to deciding whether to launch a new military operation against Iran, according to Israel’s N12. Trump said he is “considering a massive attack greater than anything before,” adding that Israel would join the operation “within two minutes” if requested.

item.title: British Pound slides as Gulf war risk fuels US Dollar rally
item.description: The Pound Sterling drops by over 0.40% against the Greenback as risk aversion weighs on most G8 currencies amid the escalation of the Middle East conflict and growing speculation of an extended US campaign against Iran. The GBP/USD trades at 1.3313 after reaching a daily high at 1.3393.

item.title: Crude Oil stops trading the headlines and starts trading the war
item.description: Crude Oil is staging the kind of one-day advance that usually arrives strapped to a flash headline, and the wires have duly supplied several, but the tape refuses to behave like a reaction.

item.title: Japanese Yen falls near multi-decade low
item.description: USD/JPY trades above163.90 on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) strengthens following significantly better-than-expected United States (US) labor market data.

item.title: United States: PCE Methodology tweaks seen as marginal – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Eli Nir and Oscar Munoz analyze upcoming BEA methodology changes to United States (US) Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index inflation for portfolio management, legal services, and computer software & accessories.

item.title: WTI rallies more than 5% as Middle East supply risks deepen
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude Oil rallies more than 5% on Thursday as hostilities between the US and Iran deepen supply risks. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $90.50 per barrel, its highest level since June 11.

item.title: European Central Bank: Hiking cycle continues at slower pace – Nordea
item.description: Nordea strategists Jan von Gerich, Tuuli Koivu and Anders Svendsen note that the European Central Bank (ECB) kept its deposit rate at 2.25% but signalled further tightening. They still forecast three additional 25bp hikes, now at a quarterly pace, taking the deposit rate to 3% by March 2027.

item.title: Natural Gas: High prices sustain European power – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Florence Schmit notes TTF natural gas has risen above €60/MWh as Middle Eastern supply disruptions intensify.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Hike pricing questioned – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Gennadiy Goldberg and Molly Brooks note that market pricing for Fed hikes has risen alongside higher Oil prices and US-Iran tensions, but they judge a July move as unlikely.

item.title: Euro slips against British Pound as ECB keeps interest rates unchanged
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades under pressure against the British Pound (GBP) as traders assess the European Central Bank’s (ECB) latest monetary policy announcement.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Slightly stronger MXN outlook – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank strategist Michael Pfister argues that Banxico’s recent rate cuts were broadly justified by moderating inflation and Mexico’s weakening economy, leaving little reason for the central bank to tighten policy despite markets pricing in roughly three rate hikes.

item.title: ECB Press Conference: Lagarde speaks on policy outlook after leaving key rates unchanged
item.description: Christine Lagarde, President of the European Central Bank (ECB), explains the ECB's decision to leave key rates unchanged at the July policy meeting and responds to questions from the press.

item.title: Lagarde speech: Some asked whether we should consider a hike
item.description: Christine Lagarde, President of the European Central Bank (ECB), explains the ECB's decision to leave key rates unchanged at the July policy meeting and responds to questions from the press.

item.title: Lagarde speech: Energy shock could intensify further
item.description: Christine Lagarde, President of the European Central Bank (ECB), explains the ECB's decision to leave key rates unchanged at the July policy meeting and responds to questions from the press.

item.title: United Kingdom: Risks for Sterling – ING
item.description: ING’s economists describe United Kingdom (UK) public finances as strained by rising spending pressures and high debt interest, despite ongoing fiscal consolidation via frozen tax thresholds and falling gilt issuance.

item.title: Lagarde speech: Indicators suggest economic activity will remain modest
item.description: Christine Lagarde, President of the European Central Bank (ECB), explains the ECB's decision to leave key rates unchanged at the July policy meeting and responds to questions from the press.
